title: Officers stand by their actions
article: Rob Harrison, a spokesman for Stochmal's widow, Shannon, told reporters she also believes police did what had to be done in a very difficult situation that tragic night on Sept. 1, 2001.

"I think that is a night that a lot of people have relived over and over again. They say hindsight is 20/20, but you know you can't change what is done. And people have to go into a situation and do the best job that they possibly can," Harrison said.

Const. Cory Culling and his partner Const. Gary Giroux were among the officers who responded to a 9-1-1 call to Stochmal's Uplands home minutes after the 35-year-old Regina man, who has a bipolar disorder, fatally stabbed his nine-year-old son, Justin.

Jurors heard that it took six officers to secure and control a struggling and raving Stochmal. They heard how police used verbal commands, pepper spray, and pressure point control tactics as they tried to calm and gain control of Stochmal, who was exhibiting "super human" strength as he struggled with police. Eventually the officers hog-tied his hands and feet behind his back, at which point Stochmal became compliant and "the fight went out of him," Giroux said.

"The minimal amount of force was used to get him under control and take him into custody. I've never seen my shift work so efficiently and professionally as they did that night," Giroux told the coroner's inquest.

Lawyer Pauline Duncan, who represents Stochmal's parents, said they understand the safety issue. Their concern, she said, rests with the fact that once their son was subdued police never checked to see if he was experiencing any medical distress.

"The testimony of the officers is quite clear that after one point he gave up the fight and then it seems that they paid no attention to him whatsoever. There was no assessment to see if he was breathing or if he had a heart rate.... and that concerns us," Duncan told reporters.
"It is certainly our view that the officers did the best they could in the situation that they were presented with, but their training was woefully inadequate given what they had to face," she said.
The inquest process is designed to maybe come up with recommendations that will help to make things better if it happens again, Harrison said.
Lawyer Aaron Fox, who represents the individual police officers, told reporters the evidence is pretty clear they had to take control of the situation and there is nothing to suggest to the contrary.

"We are dealing with a situation that is unbelievably volatile and had been extremely tragic before they even got there, and they performed their duties, which was to take control. That really is the bottom line in this," Fox said, noting their first priority is to gain physical control of the individual.

Jurors heard evidence that when police discovered Stochmal wasn't breathing and had no pulse as he was being placed in the police cruiser, they took immediate action and begin CPR. However, attempts to revive him failed.
